title: Derived units in base-unit form practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, values and figure briefs are newly authored. The mapped P2 leaves ground base-unit expansion, rearrangement of supplied relationships, charge as A s and cancellation of powers. Whole-question contexts were reviewed to isolate the t01 unit demand without requiring later-topic physics.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct prior-lesson retrieval, recognition of familiar derived units, single-step quotient reasoning, unfamiliar-constant simplification, linked force-energy-power derivation, multi-base electrical-unit derivation, then a mixed prefix-conversion and power application

questions.prompt: From the previous lesson, convert 4.8 ms to seconds and state the SI base quantity measured by a duration.
Which is the SI base-unit form of force?
Density is mass divided by volume. Which is its SI base-unit form?
A supplied model is F = kAv, where force F has unit kg m s^-2, area A has unit m^2 and speed v has unit m s^-1. Which is the SI base-unit form of k?
Use the supplied relationships to express energy and power in SI base-unit form.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Energy transferred is force multiplied by distance. Starting from N = kg m s^-2, derive the SI base-unit form of the joule, J.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Power is energy transferred divided by time. Use your base-unit form of J to derive the SI base-unit form of the watt, W.

questions.prompt: A constant epsilon appears in the supplied relationship F = Q1Q2 / (4 pi r^2 epsilon). Here F is force, Q1 and Q2 are charges and r is distance. Treat 4 pi as having no unit.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use charge = current x time to state the SI base-unit form of charge.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Rearrange the supplied relationship and determine the SI base-unit form of epsilon. Show how the powers are simplified.

questions.prompt: The data card shows the energy transferred by a small heater and the transfer time. Use 1 min = 60 s and power = energy transferred / time.

figure.purpose: Present prefixed source data clearly while requiring the learner to perform both conversion and base-unit reasoning
figure.brief: Create an original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular data card headed heater test. Show energy transferred: 3.6 kJ and transfer time: 2.0 min in separate rows. Do not include converted values, a formula, working or an answer.
figure.alt_text: A heater-test data card gives an energy transfer of 3.6 kilojoules and a time of 2.0 minutes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Convert the energy to J and the time to s.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean power transferred by the heater in W.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Express the unit W in SI base-unit form.
